identification.sponsor: Dr. Karim Naguib — Co-Founder & CTO, EduTech Dynamics

objectives.business_case:
EduTech Dynamics has identified a significant gap in project management education. University students, postgraduate candidates, and CAPM/PMP exam candidates lack access to an integrated, interactive tool that covers the full quantitative PM curriculum with step-by-step educational scaffolding.

Commercial alternatives (Microsoft Project, Oracle Primavera P6) are prohibitively expensive and operationally complex for educational settings. Free tools are fragmented and cover single techniques only. No existing open-source tool provides the complete PM curriculum with worked solutions and dual UG/PG learning modes.

The total investment of EGP 1,195,000 delivers an estimated 5-year NPV of +EGP 85,480 at a 10% discount rate (IRR ≈ 12.4%, Payback Period ≈ 3.8 years). Non-financial benefits include brand establishment in the MENA academic market, academic publication opportunities, and internal technical capability building.

Full analysis: PMHE-2025-BC-001
objectives.objectives:
O1: Deliver a fully operational desktop application covering all planned PM topic areas by 2026-08-15 (24 functional tabs, all tests passing).

O2: Support UG and PG learning modes with educational scaffolding in all calculation tabs by 2026-08-15 (worked solutions and Try It Yourself mode).

O3: Deploy a production web application at a stable public URL by 2026-07-31 (<3s load time, 99%+ uptime over 30-day measurement).

O4: Publish a standalone Windows executable and PyPI package by 2026-08-31 (both distribution channels verified).

O5: Achieve a comprehensive automated test suite by 2026-09-15 (≥ 800 passing tests, zero critical defects).

O6: Deliver a complete reference sample project by 2026-09-30 (loadable in-app, consistent across all 24 tabs).
objectives.success_criteria:
1. All 24 application tabs function correctly in both UG and PG modes.
2. All EVM KPIs produce verified correct results matching manual calculations.
3. The reference sample project loads without errors and populates all tabs.
4. The Windows executable launches on a clean Windows 10 machine without Python.
5. PyPI package installs and launches without errors.
6. Web application health endpoint returns 200.
7. Automated test suite reports ≥ 800 passing tests with zero critical failures.
8. All worked solution generators produce educationally correct step-by-step outputs.
9. Project is formally closed with lessons learned captured and approved.

scope.in_scope:
Desktop Application:
• Python/Tkinter application with 24 educational tabs in 5 collapsible groups
• Calculation engines: CPM, PERT, EVM (16 KPIs), Risk Analysis, Monte Carlo Simulation, Project Crashing, Resource Leveling, RCPS, Financial Analysis (6 metrics), Cost Estimation (7 techniques), Factor Scoring (3 models), Three-Point Estimation, AON/AOA Networks
• Strategic tools: SWOT, PESTEL, WBS, RACI Matrix, Project Charter, DPCI Assessment, Dashboard
• Educational features: worked solutions, Try It Yourself, RAG KPI coding, UG/PG mode toggle
• Project file management (.pmproj format), demo datasets, chart export

Web Application:
• Angular frontend with core calculation access
• FastAPI backend with SQLAlchemy database
• Render.com cloud deployment

Distribution:
• Windows executable via PyInstaller (--onedir, AV-safe manifest)
• PyPI package (pip install pmhelper)
• GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline

Educational Content:
• Reference sample project (PMHelper_Edu Development Project — this document set)
• In-app demos: UG Small/Medium/Large, PG Small/Medium/Large
• Standalone V2 calculator demonstrations for all individual tabs
scope.out_of_scope:
• Mobile application (iOS or Android)
• LMS integration (Moodle, Canvas, Blackboard)
• Arabic-language user interface
• Premium subscription or paid feature tiers in initial release
• Dedicated server infrastructure (cloud only)
• macOS or Linux installer packages
• Real-time multi-user collaboration
• Database-backed project storage for the desktop edition

scope.assumptions:
A1: GitHub Copilot licence available throughout the project.
A2: Render.com starter tier is sufficient for initial deployment.
A3: Python 3.8+ compatibility is sufficient for target academic environments.
A4: Windows 10+ remains the dominant OS in university computer labs.
A5: PyPI publication approval is straightforward for an open-source educational package.
A6: The lead developer can sustain the required development pace with AI assistance.
A7: The Angular frontend can reuse Python logic via the FastAPI backend.
scope.constraints:
C1: Product must be usable by the 2026–2027 academic year — hard deadline 2026-09-30.
C2: Total expenditure cannot exceed EGP 1,195,000 (all reserves included).
C3: Maximum 2.0 FTE equivalent — no additional full-time hires.
C4: Desktop application must use Python 3.8+ and Tkinter only.
C5: Primary target platform is Windows 10+ 64-bit.
C6: Must be released under the MIT Licence.
C7: Desktop application must function fully offline.

schedule.phases:
Phase 1 — Initiation (2025-09-01 to 2025-09-08): Project kickoff, team mobilisation, environment setup.

Phase 2 — Planning (2025-09-08 to 2025-10-15): Requirements, architecture design, project management plan.

Phase 3 — V1 Development (2025-10-15 to 2026-03-25): Core calculation engines, GUI tabs (CPM, EVM, Risk, PERT, Crashing, Resources, Monte Carlo), test suite, Phase 3–7 of V1 plan.

Phase 4 — Web Development (2026-03-25 to 2026-05-15): Angular frontend, FastAPI backend, Render.com deployment.

Phase 5 — V2 Development (2026-05-15 to 2026-06-30): Three-Point, Financial, RACI, Cost Estimation, Risk Response, AOA, Resource Leveling walkthrough tabs.

Phase 6 — Distribution and Testing (2026-06-30 to 2026-08-31): PyInstaller build, PyPI publication, final QA, performance testing.

Phase 7 — Documentation and Reference Project (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-30): User documentation, reference sample project, lessons learned, project closure.

risks.known_issues: No critical issues at project initiation. The following risks have been identified in the pre-project risk assessment and are being monitored from Day 1.

risk_register.description: Lead developer becomes unavailable for an extended period (illness, resignation, or competing commitment). This is the single highest-impact risk given the 100% FTE dependency.
risk_register.impact: Critical — schedule and scope directly threatened
risk_register.response: Mitigate: Comprehensive code documentation, AI-readable codebase, GitHub commit history as knowledge base. All architectural decisions documented in DECISIONS.md. Junior developer progressively cross-trained from Month 6.

risk_register.description: Scope creep from new PM curriculum requirements added mid-project by faculty advisors or the Sponsor.
risk_register.response: Mitigate: Formal change control process enforced. PM has authority to defer new requirements to V3. All changes require written sponsor approval if > 2 days effort.

risk_register.description: Institutional adoption lower than projected in Year 1–2, reducing financial returns.
risk_register.impact: High on financial returns; low on project delivery
risk_register.response: Accept (business risk, not project risk). Monitor adoption metrics from Month 1 post-release. Free open-source model reduces adoption barrier significantly.

risk_register.description: GitHub Copilot becomes unavailable or its pricing increases beyond budget.
risk_register.response: Mitigate: Document alternative AI coding tools (Claude, GPT-4, Cursor). Budget includes subscription costs through project end.

risk_register.description: PyInstaller build fails to produce a clean executable due to library compatibility issues.
risk_register.response: Mitigate: Tested PyInstaller build pipeline early (Phase 2). Patch scripts prepared for known scipy/numpy issues. Fallback: GitHub Releases with source installation instructions.
